confidence_notes: Three web searches were used: one for the RBA rate and two for Victoria Falls food and drink prices. Most tourist prices in Victoria Falls are quoted in US dollars. The sources gave inexpensive meals at about $5–10, a draft or bottled local lager at tourist bars at about $3–5, and cappuccino at about $3 on a lodge café rate card, with aggregator figures spread widely. One undated lodge café rate card listed an Aperol spritz at $8 and house wine by the glass at $6–7. I found no current aggregated figures for cocktails or wine, so those anchors rest on that one undated venue and on usual local ratios to beer. The mid-range meal for two is inferred from per-person ranges for mid-tier tourist restaurants and is moderately uncertain. Accommodation anchors are model estimates from general knowledge only; I did not search them or check any listings. July is peak dry season in Victoria Falls, so hotel rates are pushed upward. The town has few true hostels, and backpacker lodges such as Shoestrings and Victoria Falls Backpackers serve that market, so the hostel and 1-star figures are less certain.
comparable_city_reasoning: Compared with Livingstone, Zambia, just across the river, and with other southern African safari gateway towns such as Kasane and Maun in Botswana. These are dollarised or tourist-priced markets where food and drink cost more than in the wider local economy and accommodation follows international safari-tourism demand.
